intro_script: "Welcome to the Daily Robotics Brief, I'm your host. August 18th, 2026. In robotics news, Serve Robotics is expanding its delivery network, while All Three Major US Airlines have banned humanoids due to battery fire risks. Meanwhile, Samsung is pushing its humanoid development forward with a new dedicated unit and AI advancements. We'll dive into these stories and more, bringing you the latest in robotics today."
outro_script: "Thanks for joining me on the robotic revolution! It's been a wild ride today, as Serve Robotics just served up a juicy partnership with Grubhub and Diligent rolled out its Moxi 2.0 - talk about efficient delivery! Until next time, keep on charging!"

items.title: Serve Robotics adds Grubhub to delivery network as Diligent rolls out Moxi 2.0
items.summary: Serve Robotics is expanding its autonomous delivery network through a partnership with Grubhub, adding a third major delivery platform to its network alongside Uber Eats and DoorDash. The Grubhub agreement is rolling out in Chicago, Los Angeles, and Alexandria, Virginia, with more than 100 participating restaurants in Chicago and nearly 200 in Los Angeles. Meanwhile, Diligent Robotics is launching its Moxi 2.0 mobile manipulation robot in hospitals across the US, with initial deployments in Chicago, Los Angeles, and Washington, DC.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Serve Robotics adds Grubhub to delivery network as Diligent rolls out Moxi 2.0". Serve Robotics is expanding its autonomous delivery network by partnering with Grubhub, adding a third major delivery platform to its network alongside Uber Eats and DoorDash. The Grubhub agreement is being rolled out in Chicago, Los Angeles, and Alexandria, Virginia, with over 100 participating restaurants in Chicago and nearly 200 in Los Angeles. Diligent Robotics, meanwhile, is launching its Moxi 2.0 mobile manipulation robot in hospitals across the US, with initial deployments in Chicago, Los Angeles, and Washington, DC. The Moxi 2.0 robot is designed to assist with tasks such as medication delivery and patient transport. This expansion marks significant developments in the autonomous delivery and robotics industries, highlighting the growing demand for advanced delivery solutions and the increasing adoption of mobile manipulation robots in healthcare settings.

items.title: No Robots Allowed: All Three Major US Airlines Ban Humanoids Over Battery Fire Risks
items.summary: US airlines American Airlines, Delta Air Lines, United Airlines, and Southwest Airlines have banned passengers from bringing humanoid robots that resemble humans or animals onto flights due to safety concerns over battery fire risks. Standard humanoid robots use lithium-ion batteries exceeding the FAA's maximum allowance of 160 Wh, posing catastrophic logistical and safety risks in a confined cabin. The bans explicitly close loopholes and clarify that humanoids do not qualify as emotional support devices.
items.audio_script: From Humanoids Daily, "No Robots Allowed: All Three Major US Airlines Ban Humanoids Over Battery Fire Risks". US airlines American Airlines, Delta Air Lines, United Airlines, and Southwest Airlines have banned humanoid robots from being brought onto flights due to safety concerns over battery fire risks, which pose a catastrophic threat in a confined cabin. The Federal Aviation Administration had previously established a maximum allowance of 160 Wh for lithium-ion batteries, but humanoid robots often exceed this limit, rendering them unsuitable for in-flight use. The airlines' decision to ban humanoids closes a loophole and clarifies that they do not qualify as emotional support devices.

items.title: Samsung Accelerates In-House Humanoid Development with Dedicated RX Unit and World Model AI
items.summary: Samsung is developing its own proprietary humanoid robot, integrating internal manufacturing data, custom hardware, and foundation AI models into a centralized effort. The company has established a dedicated Robotics eXperience (RX) Business Promotion Office reporting directly to CEO TM Roh and hired former Hyundai executive Lee Dong-geon to steer robotics strategy. Samsung's humanoid initiative is building a physical AI software stack combining its proprietary Gauss foundation model with new "world models" designed to simulate physical dynamics before execution.
items.audio_script: From Humanoids Daily, "Samsung Accelerates In-House Humanoid Development with Dedicated RX Unit and World Model AI." Samsung has established a dedicated Robotics eXperience Business Promotion Office directly reporting to CEO TM Roh, and has hired former Hyundai executive Lee Dong-geon to steer robotics strategy, as the company accelerates its in-house humanoid development with a dedicated RX unit and integration of internal manufacturing data, custom hardware, and foundation AI models. This centralized effort combines Samsung's proprietary Gauss foundation model with new "world models" designed to simulate physical dynamics before execution, building a physical AI software stack. Samsung's humanoid initiative marks a significant step forward in its AI development capabilities, as the company seeks to establish itself as a major player in the robotics industry.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: Never miss a backport again — automatic ABI checking for ROS 2 core repos (prototype ready)
items.summary: A prototype has been developed to automatically check the ABI compatibility of ROS 2 core repository fixes, reducing the need for manual backporting efforts. The prototype uses two GitHub Actions: libabigail-action and ros2-abi-action, which compare shared libraries using libabigail and apply the REP-0009 policy for released distros and rolling. The tool can be integrated into the ROS 2 core repos and potentially shared with community packages, with feedback and concerns welcomed.

The tool can be integrated into the ROS 2 core repos and potentially shared with community packages, with feedback and concerns welcomed. The development of this prototype marks a significant advancement in the efficiency of ROS 2 maintenance.

items.title: Schaeffler Cracks the Cost Bottleneck: Formed Strain Wave Gearboxes Target 2027 Mass Production
items.summary: Schaeffler has introduced a new high-speed forming process for strain wave gearboxes, reducing component costs by over 25% and material consumption by over 75%. This breakthrough will accelerate mass manufacturing in 2027 in Germany, followed by a global expansion to support humanoid robotics partners. The formed strain wave gearboxes complement Schaeffler's existing planetary gear actuators and secure the company's position as a Tier 1 supplier for humanoid robots.
items.audio_script: From Humanoids Daily, "Schaeffler Cracks the Cost Bottleneck: Formed Strain Wave Gearboxes Target 2027 Mass Production". Schaeffler has introduced a new high-speed forming process for strain wave gearboxes, significantly reducing component costs by over 25% and material consumption by over 75%. This breakthrough was achieved through the development of a novel forming technology that enables precise control over the gear's shape and structure, resulting in improved manufacturability and reduced waste. The new process will be implemented in time for mass production in 2027 in Germany, prior to a global expansion to support humanoid robotics partners.

items.title: Building Networks That Can Keep Up With Modern Automation
items.summary: Industrial networks must adapt to increasing automation, with many devices producing and consuming data simultaneously. Network planning is now an operational issue, as a short interruption can halt a cell or delay diagnostics. To address this, teams should map traffic patterns, not just devices, and create a network that stays predictable as equipment and production requirements evolve.
items.audio_script:
From Robotics & Automation News, "Building Networks That Can Keep Up With Modern Automation", this story highlights the critical need for industrial networks to adapt to increasing automation, revealing that a network planning approach that prioritizes traffic patterns over individual devices is crucial to maintaining predictability as equipment and production requirements evolve.

Industry experts have found that by mapping traffic patterns in addition to device placement, teams can create more resilient networks that can handle the simultaneous production and consumption of data by various devices. This approach, which involves analyzing network topology and identifying potential bottlenecks, enables the creation of a network that can maintain stability even in the face of equipment failures or unexpected changes in production demands. As a result, teams can minimize downtime and ensure that diagnostic processes can be completed efficiently.

This shift in network planning approach has significant implications for the AI and tech industry, as it underscores the growing importance of adaptability and flexibility in industrial automation systems.

items.title: Is Shipyard Welding the Right First Job for Humanoid Robots?
items.summary: Persona AI has developed a humanoid robot to focus on welding in shipyards, targeting long, linear welds that are relatively uncomplicated. This task leverages the robot's ability to perform millimeter-scale repeated motions, which robots excel at, particularly over long periods of time. Shipyards offer a compelling environment for the humanoid robot, as it can work on the ground, overhead, and through portholes, and the robot's safety concerns are lessened due to the industrial environment. The company aims to create high-fidelity simulations and collect demonstration data to expand its applications to grinding, painting, and other fabrication tasks.
items.audio_script: From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "Is Shipyard Welding the Right First Job for Humanoid Robots?" This project aims to create a humanoid robot capable of performing long, linear welds in shipyards. Persona AI has developed a humanoid robot specifically designed for this task, leveraging the robot's ability to perform millimeter-scale repeated motions, a skill robots excel at, particularly over long periods. The company has chosen shipyards as the initial target due to their industrial environment, which reduces safety concerns for the robot. The robot can work on the ground, overhead, and through portholes, allowing for a comprehensive range of tasks. By creating high-fidelity simulations and collecting demonstration data, Persona AI plans to expand its applications to grinding and painting, further enhancing the robot's capabilities.

items.title: Intermittent swimming promotes the energy efficiency of fish-like robot movements
items.summary: Researchers developed a larval zebrafish-inspired robotic platform (ZBot) to investigate the energy efficiency of intermittent swimming compared to continuous swimming. They found that intermittent bout-and-glide swimming reduces energy consumption across all achievable velocities, especially in viscous fluid regimes. The team proposed the "actuator efficiency" hypothesis, suggesting that intermittent swimming enhances the transfer of energy from electricity to kinematic tail movements, allowing actuators to operate in more energy-efficient regimes.
items.audio_script: From Robohub, "Intermittent swimming promotes the energy efficiency of fish-like robot movements," researchers have developed a larval zebrafish-inspired robotic platform, known as ZBot, to investigate the energy efficiency of intermittent swimming compared to continuous swimming. The team found that intermittent bout-and-glide swimming reduces energy consumption across all achievable velocities, especially in viscous fluid regimes. By analyzing the energy transfer between the actuator and kinematic tail movements, the researchers proposed the "actuator efficiency" hypothesis, suggesting that intermittent swimming enhances the efficiency of energy transfer, allowing actuators to operate in more energy-efficient regimes.

items.title: SpotlessGS: Relightable 3D Gaussian Splatting under Dynamic Illumination for Robotic Perception
items.summary: Robots in dark or poorly lit environments rely on onboard lights, producing uneven illumination that degrades perception tasks. The authors extend Dark Gaussian Splatting (DarkGS) to create a more accurate and flexible relightable 3D reconstruction framework. This framework jointly optimizes lighting parameters within the Gaussian Splatting framework and incorporates a low-frequency illumination model based on spherical harmonics and an MLP-based Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Function (BRDF) to model non-Lambertian reflectance.

items.title: MISTac: A Vision-Based Tactile Sensor for Minimally Invasive Surgery
items.summary: MISTac, a high resolution vision-based tactile sensor, has been developed for minimally invasive surgery. The sensor has a replaceable sensor tip with a diameter of 8 mm and can resolve forces as little as 24.3 mN. It has been shown to be usable in minimally invasive surgery through an in vivo study, achieving an aggregate accuracy of ~84% in a tissue classification task. The sensor is now open-sourced for potential use in aiding surgeons during minimally invasive surgery.

items.title: Modeling and Control of an Eel-Inspired Soft Robot for Design Optimization
items.summary: A simulation model of an eel-inspired soft robot for anguilliform swimming is presented, using a Finite Element Method (FEM) model of an elastic rod to capture the soft materials of the robotic fish. The model is coupled with a hydrodynamic force model to simulate the behavior of the soft robot in water. The results show that slightly asymmetric designs are advantageous, offering comparable swimming velocities but greater maneuverability.

items.title: Real-time Estimator of Actuator Control and Health (REACH) on an Eel-Inspired Soft Robot
items.summary: A real-time estimator of actuator control and health (REACH) algorithm for an eel-inspired soft robot is developed to accurately estimate actuator functionality in harsh underwater environments. The algorithm employs a soft robot model, sigma point filter, and formal statistical hypothesis test to capture nonlinearities and changes over time. REACH is evaluated using three sensor types (GPS, IMU, and Bend Sensor) and demonstrates that both bend sensor and IMU are adequate choices, with minimal differences in performance across three swimming gaits.

items.title: Geometry-Aware Online Mapping for 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM
items.summary: Recent 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has enabled efficient photorealistic view synthesis, but its offline reconstruction heuristics can become brittle under online SLAM's incremental map growth. Researchers proposed three geometry-aware methods for online mapping, including transmittance-preserving densification, camera-aware scale initialization, and error-guided densification, which improve rendering quality with negligible overhead.

items.title: From Continuous Design to Delay-Aware Discrete Synthesis: Guaranteed High-Bandwidth Joint Control for PMSM Drives
items.summary: Researchers have developed a task-aware, delay-extended discrete-time joint model for PMSM drives, enabling the direct synthesis of a discrete PI current controller with prescribed bandwidth and delay guarantees. The framework analyzes the minimum required sampling frequency, controller gains, and DC-link voltage needed to satisfy motor and joint performance, resulting in reduced sampling-frequency and DC-link-voltage requirements.

items.title: SkillComposer: Learning Reusable Skills for Natural-Language Robot Programming
items.summary: SkillComposer is an interactive natural-language robot programming system that learns reusable program abstractions. It uses a generate-test architecture with large language models (LLMs) to iteratively generate and revise robot programs before execution. Successful programs are stored and processed by an online library-learning algorithm that compresses recurring function sequences into reusable macro skills. Evaluations show that evaluator-guided generation and learned abstractions improve success rates and usability in natural-language robot programming.

items.title: GaussMemory: Task-Driven 3D Gaussian Scene Memory for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: GaussMemory, a task-driven 3D Gaussian scene memory, is proposed for long-horizon robotic manipulation, enabling a robot to actively learn how to remember objects and update its memory. It leverages 3D Gaussian Splatting as a persistent geometric substrate. GaussMemory outperforms existing memory systems in various benchmarks, including LIBERO and VLABench.
